GPT-6.1 Terra, Muse Wonder and other new provider models, a seven-day weekly quota outlook, and dashboard improvements for account errors and installed iOS apps. Codex capacity errors also leave other sessions able to work.

## Changes since v0.9.0

- **Patched compression dependencies.** Updated `zstd` to 0.14.3, `zstd-safe` to 8.2.0 and `zstd-sys` to 2.1.2, resolving the dependency audit findings for stream-context reuse, legacy-frame decompression, seekable offsets and the WebAssembly allocator shim. Usage storage stays on the same format and database schema.
- **New provider models.** Added GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT Image 2.5 Flare and Sunburst; Claude Haiku 5.5; Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 3.1 Flash Image and Flash Lite Image, and Nano Banana 2.1; Kimi K3.1 Pro and Pro Highspeed; Grok Imagine Image Quality and Video 1.5 Lite; and Meta Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full. Vertex gains Gemini 4 Argon. Antigravity gains its Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5 effort variants; Devin gains GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet/Haiku 5.5.
- **Model request compatibility.** Preserve supported GPT-5.6/GPT-6 and Meta `max` reasoning, use Gemini 4 thinking levels, and apply Haiku 5.5 adaptive-thinking and Kimi K3.1 request rules. Meta's disabled reasoning maps to `minimal`; choosing Wonder's reasoning effort never changes it into Wonder Full. Account discovery and explicit capability settings still determine effective limits and availability.
- **Updated cost estimates.** Bundled pricing catalog `2026-10-27.2` adds Terra and Muse Wonder Standard rates, including applicable caching and service-tier rules. Wonder Full remains unpriced because it has no published pay-as-you-go rate.
- **Weekly quota outlook.** Providers with multiple enabled subscriptions get a seven-day estimate of their lowest combined weekly reserve, using recent observed quota consumption and scheduled resets. The dashboard distinguishes expected coverage, low reserve and a projected quota gap. During the initial six hours of learning, it shows current combined quota when complete readings are available. History survives restarts and quota resets; stale or missing data makes the forecast unavailable.
- **Clear saved account errors.** Dismiss a reviewed error from the account drawer or detail page, with updates across open dashboards. Clearing makes no provider request and preserves cooldowns, quota, counters and request history. New failures appear again. Temporary connection errors now also expire after 30 seconds on idle accounts.
- **Dashboard refresh and reset times.** Installed iOS apps support pull-to-refresh. Individual quota meters show countdowns to provider-reported resets, with the full reset time on hover.
- **Codex capacity and session recovery.** Provider-capacity 429s retry on the same account after 1 and 3 seconds without pausing its model for other sessions. A session whose account is cooling down receives a retryable 429 when no alternative is free, rather than a misleading model-not-found 404.

## Upgrading

- From v0.9.0, the usage database remains on schema 5; no database migration is introduced.
- Muse Wonder Full is a separate Muse Code subscription model requiring upstream eligibility on Power Usage or Maximum Usage. Default pay-as-you-go accounts neither list nor route it; explicit model mappings can describe other account entitlements.
- Weekly forecasts need six hours of continuous observations after upgrading. They estimate weekly capacity under recent demand; bursts, session affinity, five-hour/model limits and provider availability can still restrict individual requests. Future banked resets are not assumed.

See the [model review and source evidence](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.10.1/docs/model-support-2026-10-27.md) and [weekly outlook calculation](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.10.1/docs/weekly-outlook.md) for details.

[Full comparison with v0.9.0](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/compare/v0.9.0...v0.10.1).
